newsitem.title: JAPAN: JAPAN DOMESTIC WPI SEEN STABLE--BOJ.
newsitem.headline: JAPAN DOMESTIC WPI SEEN STABLE--BOJ.

text.p: Japan's domestic wholesale prices are expected to remain stable in the coming months, a Bank of Japan official told reporters on Friday.
"I don't think the situation will change (August onwards). We expect prices to remain stable," the BOJ official said.
Japan's domestic wholesale price index rose 2.0 percent in July from a year earlier, and rose 0.2 percent from a month ago.
The BOJ official attributed July's 0.2 percent rise from a month earlier to higher electricity fees, which are implemented during the July to September period.
The domestic WPI fell 0.1 percent in May from the month earlier and also slipped 0.1 percent in June from the previous month.
The fall in import prices for July from a month ago was mainly due to lower crude oil prices, he added.
"There is no change in the trend. The July data is showing stable moves in prices," he said.
